# Adjudication Task — Chapter 328

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃328화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|꺼으윽, 꺽.
  6|
  7|쩍 벌어진 목젖에서 핏물이 울컥거리며 솟구친다.
  8|
  9|허준은 버둥거리며 자신의 목을 움켜잡았지만 이미 늦었다.
 10|
 11|주화란의 일검(一劍)은 빠르고 정확했고, 한 치의 실수도 없이 목적을 이룬 뒤였다.
 12|
 13|“크륵…….”
 14|
 15|그건 죽어 가는 자의 단말마(斷末摩)였다.
 16|
 17|무슨 말을 하고 싶었던 걸까. 억울하다? 살려 달라? 아니면 죽어서까지 널 저주하겠다?
 18|
 19|피가래 끓는 소리를 내며 벙긋거리던 허준의 입술이 우뚝 굳었다.
 20|
 21|발버둥 치던 사지에 힘이 빠지고, 수많은 감정으로 얼룩진 채 주화란을 바라보던 눈동자에서는 빛이 꺼졌다.
 22|
 23|하아아…….
 24|
 25|그가 이승에서 내뱉은 마지막 숨결이 허공으로 흩어진다.
 26|
 27|군자검 주호군의 의형제이자 삼십 년간 용봉표국에 몸담았던 총표두 허준은 그렇게 죽었다.
 28|
 29|한때 자신을 혈육처럼 따르던 질녀(姪女)의 손에 의해.
 30|
 31|“……허 숙부.”
 32|
 33|작게 흘러나온 목소리. 주화란의 뒷모습은 어쩐지 황량해 보였다.
 34|
 35|숨이 끊긴 허준을 잠시간 내려다보던 그녀가 이윽고 천천히 돌아섰다.
 36|
 37|용봉표국 소속의 표사들을 스쳐 지나간 흑요석 같은 눈동자가 외인(外人)들을 향했다.
 38|
 39|한 사람, 한 사람. 그리고 마지막으로 나를 바라본 주화란이 모두를 향해 포권지례를 올렸다.
 40|
 41|“용봉표국의 소국주 주화란이 강호의 선배님들 앞에서 결례를 범했습니다.”
 42|
 43|아픔은 종종 인간을 성숙하게 만들고는 한다. 나는 그녀가 이번 일을 통해 한 단계 성장해졌기를 바랐다.
 44|
 45|‘예상보다 덤덤해 보여서 다행이기는 한데…….’
 46|
 47|뭔가 분위기가 좀, 껄끄럽단 말이지.
 48|
 49|그런 생각을 하고 있을 때, 뭔가가 내 발을 꾸욱 밟았다.
 50|
 51|시선을 내려보니 여인이 신는 화려한 당혜(唐鞋)다.
 52|
 53|내가 알기로 여기서 이런 걸 신을 만한 사람은 단 한 명밖에 없지.
 54|
 55|의문 담긴 눈으로 바라보자 월화가 눈짓으로 좌우를 가리켰다.
 56|
 57|그제야 느껴지는 사람들의 시선들.
 58|
 59|어느새 양옆으로 쫙 갈라진 이들이 나를 뚫어져라 바라보고 있다.
 60|
 61|그리고 그 끝에 포권을 취하고 있는 주화란.
 62|
 63|‘……뭔데, 이거.’
 64|
 65|내 얼굴에 뭐라도 묻었나?
 66|
 67|당황해하는 내게 월화가 들릴락 말락 한 목소리로 속삭였다.
 68|
 69|“진 공자가 한마디 해요.”
 70|
 71|“예?”
 72|
 73|“주 소저가 인사했잖아요. 대표로 받아 줘야지.”
 74|
 75|“아니, 그걸 왜 내가 해요.”
 76|
 77|“얼른. 주 소저 기다리다가 늙겠다.”
 78|
 79|“…….”
 80|
 81|그래, 그사이에 10초 정도 늙긴 했네.
 82|
 83|화산파의 유력 대선 후보, 거지 왕자 궁기방, 하오문 섬서 지부장까지 두고 왜 내가 말해야 하는지는 모르겠지만, 일단 떨떠름한 얼굴로 고개를 꾸벅 숙였다.
 84|
 85|“결례는 무슨. 그리고 저는 강호의 선배 같은 거 아니니까 막 대하셔도 되는데요.”
 86|
 87|“그럴 리 있겠습니까.”
 88|
 89|고개를 든 주화란이 차분하게 말했다.
 90|
 91|“진 대협과 여러 선배님은 용봉표국의 은인들이십니다. 여러분들의 도움이 없었다면 저희 용봉표국은 큰 곤욕을 치렀을 것이고…… 배반자를 처단하지도 못했겠지요.”
 92|
 93|마지막 한마디를 덧붙인 주화란의 표정에 씁쓸함이 스친다.
 94|
 95|그녀도 스스로 그것을 느꼈는지, 이어지는 목소리에는 한층 힘이 실렸다.
 96|
 97|“오늘 입은 은혜는 반드시 갚겠습니다.”
 98|
 99|별거 아니었는데요, 라고 하기에는 확실히 나와 여러 문파의 도움이 컸다. 주화란과 용봉표국 입장에서는 백번 절해도 모자란 수준이다.
100|
101|‘아무리 그래도 대협 소리 듣는 건 좀.’
102|
103|소협도 아직 오글거리는데, 한 단계 진화해 버렸다.
104|
105|나는 어쩐지 수염을 길러야 할 것 같은 기분을 느끼며 말을 돌렸다.
106|
107|“은혜는 저 말고 다른 분들께 갚으시고, 그보다 이제 어쩌실 건가요?”
108|
109|“우선 시신을 수습하고 표국으로 돌아갈 생각이에요. 해결해야 할 일이 많아서요.”
110|
111|“엄청 바쁘시겠네.”
112|
113|의식불명인 아버지 대신 표국을 총괄하는 주화란이다.
114|
115|길었던 표행의 뒤처리만으로도 하루가 금방 갈 텐데, 다이나믹한 사건들까지 잇따랐으니 몸이 열 개라도 부족할 것이 분명했다.
116|
117|내 말에 고개를 끄덕인 주화란이 입을 열었다.
118|
119|“그래도 진 대협 일행을 대접할 만큼의 여유는 있습니다.”
120|
121|“여유가 있다니 그것참 다행…… 예?”
122|
123|“진 대협께서는 저와 식솔들을 구해 주신 은인이십니다. 제대로 된 대접 한번 없이 떠나보낼 수는 없지요.”
124|
125|“어, 주 소저. 그게요.”
126|
127|“혹시, 많이 바쁘신가요?”
128|
129|바쁘지. 상당히 바쁘지.
130|
131|적천강의 치료 기한은 최소 6개월에서 최대 8개월.
132|
133|나는 그 안에 광활한 사천 땅을 뒤져 신의(神醫)라는 정체불명의 인물을 찾아야 한다.
134|
135|‘하남에서 섬서까지 걸린 시간은 일주일. 사천에 당도하려면 아무리 빨라도 또다시 일주일을 이동해야 한다.’
136|
137|그마저도 최대한 신법을 발휘했을 때의 이야기다.
138|
139|신의는 모든 것이 베일에 싸인 인물. 얼만큼의 시간이 소요될지는 누구도 예측할 수 없다.
140|
141|그것이 서안에서 고작 하루를 보내고도 마음이 불안해지는 이유였다.
142|
143|‘오늘도 늦었고.’
144|
145|해가 중천에 뜬 지 오래. 종남파와 얽히는 바람에 상당한 시간을 지체했으니 지금부터라도 발에 불이 나도록 뛰어야 했다.
146|
147|그런데…….
148|
149|“아뇨. 안 바빠요.”
150|
151|나도 모르게 입이 열리더니, 저딴 대답이 튀어나와 버렸다.
152|
153|방금 무슨 일이 벌어진 거지. 이건 원래 하려던 말의 정반대잖아.
154|
155|순간 멍해진 내게 주화란이 조심스럽게 묻는다.
156|
157|“진 대협, 정말 괜찮으신 거 맞아요? 혹시 급한 일이 있으시다면 다음으로 미뤄도 괜찮은데.”
158|
159|감사합니다. 먼저 말 꺼내 주셔서 정말 감사합니다.
160|
161|눈치 빠르고 똑똑한 그녀답다. 가려운 곳을 긁어 주는 말에 나는 망설임 없이 대답했다.
162|
163|“아무리 급해도 밥 한 끼 같이 못 먹겠습니까.”
164|
165|“네에.”
166|
167|“안 그래도 힘을 써서 배고프던 차였는데 잘됐네요. 갑시다.”
168|
169|병신인가, 진짜. 사천에 가야지 용봉표국을 왜 가.
170|
171|하지만 정신을 차렸을 때는 이미 지게를 짊어진 후였다.
172|
173|내심 한숨을 푹 내쉰 그때, 이 모든 상황에서 동떨어져 있던 한 사람이 눈에 들어왔다.
174|
175|물끄러미 바라보자 그가 먼저 입을 연다.
176|
177|“왜, 무슨 할 말이라도 있나?”
178|
179|초면에 반말이 이렇게 자연스럽게 들리기는 처음인데.
180|
181|어쨌든 저쪽에서 먼저 말을 놔 주니 나도 편했다.
182|
183|“그냥. 당신은 안 가나 싶어서.”
184|
185|“일 없다.”
186|
187|“그럼 만들어.”
188|
189|“……?”
190|
191|“어차피 시간 남아도는 거 아니까, 대화나 좀 나누자고.”
192|
193|“대화?”
194|
195|“어, 대화.”
196|
197|눈썹을 치켜세우며 날 바라보던 그, 송일섬이 비스듬히 기대고 있던 몸을 바로 세웠다.
198|
199|
200|
201|* * *
202|
203|
204|
205|초봄. 쨍쨍했던 태양은 용봉표국에 도착한 지 두 시진도 채 되지 않아 서산 뒤로 모습을 감췄다.
206|
207|호롱불이 밝혀진 접객실의 탁자 위에는 진수성찬이 차려졌고, 눈을 휘둥그레 뜬 청풍과 궁기방은 허겁지겁 음식들을 입 안으로 쑤셔 넣었다.
208|
209|“쩝쩝. 으닌. 이거 마시써요. 쩝쩝쩝.”
210|
211|“……많이 먹어. 가급적 말은 하지 말고.”
212|
213|맛있어 보이긴 했다.
214|
215|청풍이 굳이 입 안에 든 걸 보여 주기 전까지는.
216|
217|“와구와구. 이 표국 음식 잘하네. 소국주. 혹시 본 방의 식구들에게도 남는 음식을 나눠 줄 수 있겠소?”
218|
219|궁기방, 저 자식은 진짜 뼛속까지 거지다.
220|
221|고기 위주로 학살 중인 녀석을 향해 주화란이 고개를 끄덕였다.
222|
223|“물론이죠. 배가 고프면 얼마든지 찾아오라고 하세요.”
224|
225|“오, 얼마든지?”
226|
227|“……그렇다고 너무 많이는 어렵고요.”
228|
229|섬서성에 있는 개방도만 몰려와도 합의금으로 받을 은자 사십만 냥이 식비로 털릴 거다.
230|
231|궁기방은 누런 이를 드러내며 씩 웃었다.
232|
233|“걱정 마시오. 걱정하는 일 없도록 잘 일러두겠소.”
234|
235|그나마 멀쩡하게 식사를 하고 있던 혁무진이 속삭였다.
236|
237|“저렇게 말하니까 더 걱정되는데요.”
238|
239|“그러게.”
240|
241|이러다가 용봉표국이 종남파가 아니라 개방 때문에 망하는 거 아니냐.
242|
243|내심 주의를 줘야겠다 다짐하는 내게 주화란이 말을 걸었다.
244|
245|“다른 분들이 오시지 않은 게 아쉽네요.”
246|
247|“그러게요. 음식도 맛있는데.”
248|
249|우리 일행을 제외한 다른 사람들, 그러니까 백무성과 흑걸개, 월화는 모두 초대에 응하지 않았다.
250|
251|왜 그런지는 모르겠지만, 월화가 두 사람을 지그시 째려보자 말을 바꾼 것 같기도 하다.
252|
253|뭐 어쨌든…….
254|
255|“그런 것치고는 많이 안 드시는데요?”
256|
257|“아뇨, 맛있던데요. 보세요. 밥도 두 그릇이나 비운 거.”
258|
259|“이상하다. 그런데 왜 적게 드신 것 같지.”
260|
261|“상대적인 거죠. 쟤들 보세요. 음식이랑 정마대전 치르고 있잖아요.”
262|
263|쿰척쿰척!
264|
265|와구와구!
266|
267|쩝쩝쩝쩝!
268|
269|주화란이 깨달음을 얻은 사람처럼 고개를 끄덕였다.
270|
271|“아아.”
272|
273|“저랑 무진이가 정상인 겁니다. 정작 적게 먹는 사람은 저쪽이고.”
274|
275|송일섬이 무뚝뚝한 목소리로 대꾸했다.
276|
277|“십 년 동안 말했지만, 여기 음식은 간이 너무 짜다. 맵고 짠 음식은 자극이 심하고 몸을 무겁게 하지.”
278|
279|“갑자기 한 사람이 생각나네. 이 자리에 있었으면 널 국자로 때려죽였을 텐데.”
280|
281|“누굴 말하는 거지?”
282|
283|“그런 분이 계셔. 한 대 맞으면 비명이 절로 나올걸. 나도 지금까지 오지게 맞았지. 희한하게 한 번도 못 피하겠더라고.”
284|
285|“진 대협, 사실인가요?”
286|
287|“네가 말이냐?”
288|
289|주화란은 깜짝 놀라 반문했고, 송일섬의 눈동자가 번뜩였다.
290|
291|“태을무정검을 쓰러트린 네가 그리 말할 정도라면…… 실로 엄청난 고수인 모양이군. 그분의 성함과 별호를 알려 줄 수 있겠나?”
292|
293|“김정희. 별호는 여사.”
294|
295|“으음. 들어 본 적 없다.”
296|
297|그렇겠지. 우리 엄마니까.
298|
299|나는 내색하지 않고 근엄한 어조로 말을 이었다.
300|
301|“아무튼 그분께서 누누이 말씀하시길, 가리는 거 없이 이것저것 다 잘 먹어야 무럭무럭 큰, 아니 강해진다고 하셨지.”
302|
303|“음.”
304|
305|“그러니까 반찬 투정하지 말고 처먹어.”
306|
307|심각한 얼굴로 고민하던 송일섬이 젓가락을 들어 반찬을 집어 먹기 시작했다.
308|

Feeling as though I ought to grow a beard, I changed the subject.

[P53]
“Repay the others, not me. More importantly, what are you going to do now?”

[P54]
“We’ll recover the bodies first and return to the bureau. There’s a lot to take care of.”

[P55]
“You must be incredibly busy.”

[P56]
Ju Hwaran was managing the bureau in place of her unconscious father.

[P57]
Dealing with the aftermath of the long escort mission alone would fill her days, and after one outrageous incident after another, even ten bodies wouldn’t be enough to handle everything.

[P58]
Ju Hwaran nodded.

[P59]
“Even so, we have enough time to host Great Hero Jin and his companions.”

[P60]
“You have enough time? That’s a relief… Huh?”

[P61]
“You and your companions are Benefactors who saved me and everyone under my care. I cannot send you away without offering you proper hospitality.”

[P62]
“Um, Young Lady Ju, the thing is…”

[P63]
“Are you perhaps very busy?”

[P64]
I was busy. Extremely busy.

[P65]
Jeok Cheongang had a treatment window of six months at minimum and eight at most.

[P66]
Within that time, I had to scour the vast land of Sichuan for the mysterious person known as the Divine Physician.

[P67]
*It took us a week to get from Henan to Shaanxi. Reaching Sichuan will take at least another week, no matter how fast we travel.*

[P68]
And that was assuming I used my movement technique to the fullest.

[P69]
Everything about the Divine Physician was shrouded in mystery. No one could predict how long it would take to find him.

[P70]
That was why spending even a single day in Xi’an had already made me anxious.

[P71]
*And it’s already late in the day.*

[P72]
The sun had passed its zenith long ago. Our entanglement with the Zhongnan Sect had cost us a considerable amount of time, so I needed to start running as though my feet were on fire.

[P73]
And yet…

[P74]
“No, I’m not busy.”

[P75]
My mouth opened of its own accord, and that ridiculous answer slipped out.

[P76]
What had just happened? That was the exact opposite of what I had meant to say.

[P77]
As I stood there dazed, Ju Hwaran cautiously asked,

[P78]
“Great Hero Jin, are you sure? If you have urgent business, we can always postpone it.”

[P79]
*Thank you. Thank you so much for saying that first.*

[P80]
Sharp and perceptive as ever. She had scratched exactly where it itched, and I answered without hesitation.

[P81]
“No matter how urgent it is, surely I can spare enough time to share one meal with you.”

[P82]
“Right…”

[P83]
“I was already hungry after exerting myself so much. This works out perfectly. Let’s go.”

[P84]
*Am I a fucking idiot? Seriously?*

[P85]
I needed to go to Sichuan. Why the hell was I going to the Yongbong Escort Bureau?

[P86]
But by the time I came to my senses, I had already hoisted the pack frame onto my back.

[P87]
Just as I heaved an inward sigh, I noticed someone who had remained completely detached from everything going on around him.

[P88]
When I stared at him, he spoke first.

[P89]
“What? Do you have something to say?”

[P90]
This was the first time casual speech from someone I had just met sounded so natural.

[P91]
Since he had dropped the formalities first, that made things easier for me too.

[P92]
“I was just wondering if you weren’t coming.”

[P93]
“I have no reason to.”

[P94]
“Then make one.”

[P95]
“…?”

[P96]
“I know you have plenty of time to spare, so let’s have a conversation.”

[P97]
“A conversation?”

[P98]
“Yeah. A conversation.”

[P99]
Song Ilseom raised an eyebrow at me, then pushed himself upright from where he had been leaning.

[P100]
* * *

[P101]
It was early spring. The blazing sun disappeared behind the western mountains less than two shichen after we arrived at the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P102]
Oil lamps illuminated the reception room, where a magnificent feast had been laid out across the table. Cheongpung and Gung Gibang stared wide-eyed as they crammed food into their mouths.

[P103]
“Mmph. Ben’factor. This is delicious. Mmph-mmph-mmph.”

[P104]
“…Eat as much as you want. Just try not to talk.”

[P105]
The food did look delicious.

[P106]
At least until Cheongpung went out of his way to show me what was in his mouth.

[P107]
“Gobble, gobble. This Escort Bureau sure knows how to cook. Young Bureau Head, could you give the extra food to the members of our sect as well?”

[P108]
Gung Gibang really was a beggar to the bone.

[P109]
Ju Hwaran nodded to the bastard as he continued massacring the meat dishes.

[P110]
“Of course. Tell them they can come whenever they’re hungry.”

[P111]
“Oh, whenever they’re hungry?”

[P112]
“…Not too many at once, though.”

[P113]
If every Beggars’ Sect disciple in Shaanxi Province descended on the place, all four hundred thousand silver nyang of our compensation would disappear into food costs.

[P114]
Gung Gibang grinned, baring his yellow teeth.

[P115]
“Don’t worry. I’ll make sure to explain it so you have nothing to worry about.”

[P116]
Hyuk Mujin, who was at least eating normally, whispered,

[P117]
“The way he says that makes me even more worried.”

[P118]
“You said it.”

[P119]
At this rate, the Yongbong Escort Bureau might go under because of the Beggars’ Sect instead of the Zhongnan Sect.

[P120]
I was resolving to give him a warning when Ju Hwaran spoke to me.

[P121]
“It’s a shame the others didn’t come.”

[P122]
“Yeah. The food is good, too.”

[P123]
The others in our group—Baek Museong, Heukgeol Beggar, and Wolhwa—had all declined the invitation.

[P124]
I wasn’t sure why, but the two men might have changed their answers after Wolhwa gave them a long, pointed stare.

[P125]
In any case…

[P126]
“For someone who likes the food, you aren’t eating very much.”

[P127]
“No, it’s delicious. Look. I’ve already finished two bowls of rice.”

[P128]
“That’s strange. Why does it seem as though you’ve barely eaten?”

[P129]
“It’s all relative. Look at them. They’re waging the Great Faction War against the food.”

[P130]
*Schlurp, schlurp!*

[P131]
*Gobble, gobble!*

[P132]
*Chomp, chomp, chomp!*

[P133]
Ju Hwaran nodded as though she had attained enlightenment.

[P134]
“Ah.”

[P135]
“Mujin and I are the normal ones. The person who’s actually eating very little is over there.”

[P136]
Song Ilseom replied in his usual blunt tone.

[P137]
“I’ve been saying this for ten years, but the food here is too salty. Spicy and salty dishes overstimulate the senses and weigh down the body.”

[P138]
“That reminds me of someone. If she were here, she’d beat you to death with a ladle.”

[P139]
“Who are you talking about?”

[P140]
“Someone I know. One hit from her and you’ll scream whether you mean to or not. She’s beaten the hell out of me over the years, and strangely enough, I’ve never managed to dodge her once.”

[P141]
“Great Hero Jin, is that true?”

[P142]
“You?”

[P143]
Ju Hwaran stared at me in surprise, while Song Ilseom’s eyes flashed.

[P144]
“If even you, the man who defeated the Taeeul Merciless Sword, say so… she must be an extraordinary master indeed. Can you tell me her name and epithet?”

[P145]
“Kim Jeonghee. Her epithet is Lady.”

[P146]
“Hmm. I’ve never heard of her.”

[P147]
Of course he hadn’t. She was my mother.

[P148]
Keeping my expression solemn, I continued.

[P149]
“In any case, she always said you had to eat all kinds of food without being picky if you wanted to grow big—no, strong.”

[P150]
“Hmm.”

[P151]
“So stop whining about the side dishes and fucking eat.”

[P152]
Song Ilseom pondered this with a serious expression, then picked up his chopsticks and began eating the side dishes.

[P153]
The more I watched him, the stranger his personality seemed.

[P154]
*He’s strange, but he doesn’t seem dangerous.*

[P155]
A few shichen earlier, I had briefly suspected Song Ilseom of being something very bad indeed.

[P156]
It had been a reasonable suspicion. He was an exceptional Peak master who had concealed his strength for ten years, and I had already encountered a similar case in Shanxi Province.

[P157]
*Dark Heaven.*

[P158]
The Head Elder and the Five Gates of Shanxi had lain low for decades. Perhaps that was why Song Ilseom’s behavior had reminded me of them.

[P159]
But the longer I spoke with him, the more my suspicion faded, leaving only curiosity behind.

[P160]
*What the hell is this guy?*

[P161]
His speech and manner were blunt, almost rustic, yet something about his appearance and bearing carried an odd air of refinement.

[P162]
Perhaps that was why his casual speech sounded so natural.

[P163]
*What a strange bastard.*

[P164]
I stared at Song Ilseom.

[P165]
He chewed the side dishes thoroughly, his face twisted into an exaggerated grimace. After swallowing, he spoke.

[P166]
“That look again. What is it?”

[P167]
“I was just thinking about your identity.”

[P168]
“Are you that curious?”

[P169]
“Yeah. Very.”

[P170]
Talking with this guy was like driving down a wide-open highway. That was why it felt so comfortable.

[P171]
Before long, everyone else—including Ju Hwaran—had pricked up their ears and fixed their eyes on Song Ilseom’s mouth.

[P172]
Apparently displeased by the attention, he raised an eyebrow.

[P173]
“There’s nothing special about it. I stayed at the Yongbong Escort Bureau because of a connection to the previous generation.”

[P174]
“A connection to the previous generation?”

[P175]
“To be precise, my father received a great kindness from them.”

[P176]
Huh? Wait a second. That sounded familiar, but I couldn’t quite place it.

[P177]
I turned and found Ju Hwaran staring wide-eyed at Song Ilseom.

[P178]
This was clearly the first time she had heard the story in ten years.

[P179]
“May I ask your father’s name?”

[P180]
“Song Pyosan.”

[P181]
“Song Pyosan… I’ve never heard that name.”

[P182]
“That’s hardly surprising. It happened almost fifty years ago.”

[P183]
Almost fifty years ago? Was he talking about the Great Faction War?

[P184]
Before we could ask, Song Ilseom continued as though it were nothing important.

[P185]
“The Guangdong Chen Family was forgotten long ago. The woman who survived thanks to Escort King Ju Gongsan feared the greed of martial artists, so she gave her own surname to her child. It was a wise decision.”

[P186]
I felt completely blindsided. Ju Hwaran stared at Song Ilseom with trembling eyes.

[P187]
“Then could you be…?”

[P188]
Instead of answering, Song Ilseom drew a faded jade hairpin from his robes and held it out.

[P189]
It was the only escort fee a young escort surnamed Ju had received from a heavily pregnant woman more than fifty years ago.

[P5]
Ju Hwaran’s sword had been swift and precise. Her strike had accomplished its purpose without deviating so much as an inch.

[P6]
“Grrk…”

[P7]
It was the death rattle of a dying man.

[P8]
What had he wanted to say? *This is unfair? Spare me? Or perhaps, I’ll curse you even in death?*

[P9]
Heo Jun’s lips moved soundlessly as blood rattled in his throat, then went still.

[P10]
The strength drained from his flailing limbs. His eyes, fixed on Ju Hwaran and clouded with countless emotions, lost their light.

[P11]
Haaa…

[P12]
His final breath in this world dispersed into the air.

[P13]
Heo Jun—the sworn brother of Junzi Sword Ju Hogun and the Chief Escort who had served the Yongbong Escort Bureau for thirty years—died just like that.

[P14]
At the hands of the niece who had once followed him as though he were family.

[P15]
“…Uncle Heo.”

[P16]
The words slipped quietly from Ju Hwaran’s lips. From behind, she looked strangely desolate.

[P17]
She gazed down at Heo Jun’s lifeless body for a moment, then slowly turned around.

[P18]
Her obsidian eyes passed over the escorts of the Yongbong Escort Bureau and settled on the outsiders.

[P19]
One person at a time. Finally, she looked at me, then offered everyone a formal martial salute.

[P20]
“I, Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, have been discourteous before my seniors in the martial world.”

[P21]
Pain often made people mature. I hoped this ordeal had helped her grow.

[P22]
*It’s a relief that she seems calmer than I expected, but…*

[P23]
There was an awkward edge to the air.

[P24]
As I wondered why, a foot pressed down hard on mine.

[P25]
I looked down and saw an ornate woman’s shoe.

[P26]
As far as I knew, there was only one person here who would wear something like that.

[P27]
When I gave her a questioning look, Wolhwa glanced pointedly to either side.

[P28]
Only then did I notice everyone staring at me.

[P29]
At some point, they had all split off to either side and were now looking straight at me.

[P30]
At the end of the path they had opened stood Ju Hwaran, still holding her salute.

[P31]
*…What is this?*

[P32]
Was there something on my face?

[P33]
As I stood there bewildered, Wolhwa whispered so softly I could barely hear her.

[P34]
“Young Master Jin, say something.”

[P35]
“Pardon?”

[P36]
“Young Lady Ju greeted us. You need to respond on everyone’s behalf.”

[P37]
“Why do I have to do it?”

[P38]
“Hurry. Young Lady Ju will grow old waiting.”

[P39]
“…”

[P40]
Well, she had aged about ten seconds in the meantime.

[P41]
I had no idea why I had to speak when Huashan’s leading candidate for Sect Leader, the Beggar Prince, and the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi Branch Leader were all standing right there, but I gave an awkward bow anyway.

[P42]
“There’s no need to apologize. And I’m no senior of the martial world, so you don’t have to stand on ceremony with me.”

[P43]
“How could I do that?”

[P44]
Ju Hwaran raised her head and spoke calmly.

[P45]
“Great Hero Jin and the other seniors are Benefactors of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. Without your help, we would have suffered a terrible ordeal… and we would never have been able to punish the traitor.”

[P46]
A trace of bitterness crossed her face as she added those final words.

[P47]
Perhaps she noticed it herself, because her voice grew firmer.

[P48]
“I will repay the debt we owe you today without fail.”

[P49]
I couldn’t exactly claim it had been nothing. The help provided by me and the other sects had certainly been substantial. From the perspective of Ju Hwaran and the Yongbong Escort Bureau, even a hundred bows wouldn’t have been enough.

[P50]
*Still, being called Great Hero is a little much.*

[P51]
Even Young Hero made me cringe, and now the title had evolved to the next stage.

[P52]
Feeling as though I ought to grow a beard, I changed the subject.

[P53]
“Repay the others, not me. More importantly, what are you going to do now?”

[P54]
“We’ll recover the bodies first and return to the bureau. There’s a lot to take care of.”

[P55]
“You must be incredibly busy.”

[P56]
Ju Hwaran was managing the bureau in place of her unconscious father.

[P57]
Dealing with the aftermath of the long escort mission alone would fill her days, and after one outrageous incident after another, even ten bodies wouldn’t be enough to handle everything.

[P58]
Ju Hwaran nodded.

[P59]
“Even so, we have enough time to host Great Hero Jin and his companions.”

[P60]
“You have enough time? That’s a relief… Huh?”

[P61]
“You and your companions are Benefactors who saved me and everyone under my care. I cannot send you away without offering you proper hospitality.”

[P62]
“Um, Young Lady Ju, the thing is…”

[P63]
“Are you perhaps very busy?”

[P64]
I was busy. Extremely busy.

[P65]
Jeok Cheongang had a treatment window of six months at minimum and eight at most.

[P66]
Within that time, I had to scour the vast land of Sichuan for the mysterious person known as the Divine Physician.

[P67]
*It took us a week to get from Henan to Shaanxi. Reaching Sichuan will take at least another week, no matter how fast we travel.*

[P68]
And that was assuming I used my movement technique to the fullest.

[P69]
Everything about the Divine Physician was shrouded in mystery. No one could predict how long it would take to find him.

[P70]
That was why spending even a single day in Xi’an had already made me anxious.

[P71]
*And it’s already late in the day.*

[P72]
The sun had passed its zenith long ago. Our entanglement with the Zhongnan Sect had cost us a considerable amount of time, so I needed to start running as though my feet were on fire.

[P73]
And yet…

[P74]
“No, I’m not busy.”

[P75]
My mouth opened of its own accord, and that ridiculous answer slipped out.

[P76]
What had just happened? That was the exact opposite of what I had meant to say.

[P77]
As I stood there dazed, Ju Hwaran cautiously asked,

[P78]
“Great Hero Jin, are you sure? If you have urgent business, we can always postpone it.”

[P79]
*Thank you. Thank you so much for saying that first.*

[P80]
Sharp and perceptive as ever. She had scratched exactly where it itched, and I answered without hesitation.

[P81]
“No matter how urgent it is, surely I can spare enough time to share one meal with you.”

[P82]
“Right…”

[P83]
“I was already hungry after exerting myself so much. This works out perfectly. Let’s go.”

[P84]
*Am I a fucking idiot? Seriously?*

[P85]
I needed to go to Sichuan. Why the hell was I going to the Yongbong Escort Bureau?

[P86]
But by the time I came to my senses, I had already hoisted the pack frame onto my back.

[P87]
Just as I heaved an inward sigh, I noticed someone who had remained completely detached from everything going on around him.

[P88]
When I stared at him, he spoke first.

[P89]
“What? Do you have something to say?”

[P90]
This was the first time casual speech from someone I had just met sounded so natural.

[P91]
Since he had dropped the formalities first, that made things easier for me too.

[P92]
“I was just wondering if you weren’t coming.”

[P93]
“I have no reason to.”

[P94]
“Then make one.”

[P95]
“…?”

[P96]
“I know you have plenty of time to spare, so let’s have a conversation.”

[P97]
“A conversation?”

[P98]
“Yeah. A conversation.”

[P99]
Song Ilseom raised an eyebrow at me, then pushed himself upright from where he had been leaning.

[P100]
* * *

[P101]
It was early spring. The blazing sun disappeared behind the western mountains less than two shichen after we arrived at the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P102]
Oil lamps illuminated the reception room, where a magnificent feast had been laid out across the table. Cheongpung and Gung Gibang stared wide-eyed as they crammed food into their mouths.

[P103]
“Mmph. Ben’factor. This is delicious. Mmph-mmph-mmph.”

[P104]
“…Eat as much as you want. Just try not to talk.”

[P105]
The food did look delicious.

[P106]
At least until Cheongpung went out of his way to show me what was in his mouth.

[P107]
“Gobble, gobble. This Escort Bureau sure knows how to cook. Young Bureau Head, could you give the extra food to the members of our sect as well?”

[P108]
Gung Gibang really was a beggar to the bone.

[P109]
Ju Hwaran nodded to the bastard as he continued massacring the meat dishes.

[P110]
“Of course. Tell them they can come whenever they’re hungry.”

[P111]
“Oh, whenever they’re hungry?”

[P112]
“…Not too many at once, though.”

[P113]
If every Beggars’ Sect disciple in Shaanxi Province descended on the place, all four hundred thousand silver nyang of our compensation would disappear into food costs.

[P114]
Gung Gibang grinned, baring his yellow teeth.

[P115]
“Don’t worry. I’ll make sure to explain it so you have nothing to worry about.”

[P116]
Hyuk Mujin, who was at least eating normally, whispered,

[P117]
“The way he says that makes me even more worried.”

[P118]
“You said it.”

[P119]
At this rate, the Yongbong Escort Bureau might go under because of the Beggars’ Sect instead of the Zhongnan Sect.

[P120]
I was resolving to give him a warning when Ju Hwaran spoke to me.

[P121]
“It’s a shame the others didn’t come.”

[P122]
“Yeah. The food is good, too.”

[P123]
The others in our group—Baek Museong, Heukgeol Beggar, and Wolhwa—had all declined the invitation.

[P124]
I wasn’t sure why, but the two men might have changed their answers after Wolhwa gave them a long, pointed stare.

[P125]
In any case…

[P126]
“For someone who likes the food, you aren’t eating very much.”

[P127]
“No, it’s delicious. Look. I’ve already finished two bowls of rice.”

[P128]
“That’s strange. Why does it seem as though you’ve barely eaten?”

[P129]
“It’s all relative. Look at them. They’re waging the Great Faction War against the food.”

[P130]
*Schlurp, schlurp!*

[P131]
*Gobble, gobble!*

[P132]
*Chomp, chomp, chomp!*

[P133]
Ju Hwaran nodded as though she had attained enlightenment.

[P134]
“Ah.”

[P135]
“Mujin and I are the normal ones. The person who’s actually eating very little is over there.”

[P136]
Song Ilseom replied in his usual blunt tone.

[P137]
“I’ve been saying this for ten years, but the food here is too salty. Spicy and salty dishes overstimulate the senses and weigh down the body.”

[P138]
“That reminds me of someone. If she were here, she’d beat you to death with a ladle.”

[P139]
“Who are you talking about?”

[P140]
“Someone I know. One hit from her and you’ll scream whether you mean to or not. She’s beaten the hell out of me over the years, and strangely enough, I’ve never managed to dodge her once.”

[P141]
“Great Hero Jin, is that true?”

[P142]
“You?”

[P143]
Ju Hwaran stared at me in surprise, while Song Ilseom’s eyes flashed.

[P144]
“If even you, the man who defeated the Taeeul Merciless Sword, say so… she must be an extraordinary master indeed. Can you tell me her name and epithet?”

[P145]
“Kim Jeonghee. Her epithet is Lady.”

[P146]
“Hmm. I’ve never heard of her.”

[P147]
Of course he hadn’t. She was my mother.

[P148]
Keeping my expression solemn, I continued.

[P149]
“In any case, she always said you had to eat all kinds of food without being picky if you wanted to grow big—no, strong.”

[P150]
“Hmm.”

[P151]
“So stop whining about the side dishes and fucking eat.”

[P152]
Song Ilseom pondered this with a serious expression, then picked up his chopsticks and began eating the side dishes.

[P153]
The more I watched him, the stranger his personality seemed.

[P154]
*He’s strange, but he doesn’t seem dangerous.*

[P155]
A few shichen earlier, I had briefly suspected Song Ilseom of being something very bad indeed.

[P156]
It had been a reasonable suspicion. He was an exceptional Peak master who had concealed his strength for ten years, and I had already encountered a similar case in Shanxi Province.

[P157]
*Dark Heaven.*

[P158]
The Head Elder and the Five Gates of Shanxi had lain low for decades. Perhaps that was why Song Ilseom’s behavior had reminded me of them.

[P159]
But the longer I spoke with him, the more my suspicion faded, leaving only curiosity behind.

[P160]
*What the hell is this guy?*

[P161]
His speech and manner were blunt, almost rustic, yet something about his appearance and bearing carried an odd air of refinement.

[P162]
Perhaps that was why his casual speech sounded so natural.

[P163]
*What a strange bastard.*

[P164]
I stared at Song Ilseom.

[P165]
He chewed the side dishes thoroughly, his face twisted into an exaggerated grimace. After swallowing, he spoke.

[P166]
“That look again. What is it?”

[P167]
“I was just thinking about your identity.”

[P168]
“Are you that curious?”

[P169]
“Yeah. Very.”

[P170]
Talking with this guy was like driving down a wide-open highway. That was why it felt so comfortable.

[P171]
Before long, everyone else—including Ju Hwaran—had pricked up their ears and fixed their eyes on Song Ilseom’s mouth.

[P172]
Apparently displeased by the attention, he raised an eyebrow.

[P173]
“There’s nothing special about it. I stayed at the Yongbong Escort Bureau because of a connection to the previous generation.”

[P174]
“A connection to the previous generation?”

[P175]
“To be precise, my father received a great kindness from them.”

[P176]
Huh? Wait a second. That sounded familiar, but I couldn’t quite place it.

[P177]
I turned and found Ju Hwaran staring wide-eyed at Song Ilseom.

[P178]
This was clearly the first time she had heard the story in ten years.

[P179]
“May I ask your father’s name?”

[P180]
“Song Pyosan.”

[P181]
“Song Pyosan… I’ve never heard that name.”

[P182]
“That’s hardly surprising. It happened almost fifty years ago.”

[P183]
Almost fifty years ago? Was he talking about the Great Faction War?

[P184]
Before we could ask, Song Ilseom continued as though it were nothing important.

[P185]
“The Guangdong Chen Family was forgotten long ago. The woman who survived thanks to Escort King Ju Gongsan feared the greed of martial artists, so she gave her own surname to her child. It was a wise decision.”

[P186]
I felt completely blindsided. Ju Hwaran stared at Song Ilseom with trembling eyes.

[P187]
“Then could you be…?”

[P188]
Instead of answering, Song Ilseom drew a faded jade hairpin from his robes and held it out.

[P189]
It was the only escort fee a young escort surnamed Ju had received from a heavily pregnant woman more than fifty years ago.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 328

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃328화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|꺼으윽, 꺽.
  6|
  7|쩍 벌어진 목젖에서 핏물이 울컥거리며 솟구친다.
  8|
  9|허준은 버둥거리며 자신의 목을 움켜잡았지만 이미 늦었다.
 10|
 11|주화란의 일검(一劍)은 빠르고 정확했고, 한 치의 실수도 없이 목적을 이룬 뒤였다.
 12|
 13|“크륵…….”
 14|
 15|그건 죽어 가는 자의 단말마(斷末摩)였다.
 16|
 17|무슨 말을 하고 싶었던 걸까. 억울하다? 살려 달라? 아니면 죽어서까지 널 저주하겠다?
 18|
 19|피가래 끓는 소리를 내며 벙긋거리던 허준의 입술이 우뚝 굳었다.
 20|
 21|발버둥 치던 사지에 힘이 빠지고, 수많은 감정으로 얼룩진 채 주화란을 바라보던 눈동자에서는 빛이 꺼졌다.
 22|
 23|하아아…….
 24|
 25|그가 이승에서 내뱉은 마지막 숨결이 허공으로 흩어진다.
 26|
 27|군자검 주호군의 의형제이자 삼십 년간 용봉표국에 몸담았던 총표두 허준은 그렇게 죽었다.
 28|
 29|한때 자신을 혈육처럼 따르던 질녀(姪女)의 손에 의해.
 30|
 31|“……허 숙부.”
 32|
 33|작게 흘러나온 목소리. 주화란의 뒷모습은 어쩐지 황량해 보였다.
 34|
 35|숨이 끊긴 허준을 잠시간 내려다보던 그녀가 이윽고 천천히 돌아섰다.
 36|
 37|용봉표국 소속의 표사들을 스쳐 지나간 흑요석 같은 눈동자가 외인(外人)들을 향했다.
 38|
 39|한 사람, 한 사람. 그리고 마지막으로 나를 바라본 주화란이 모두를 향해 포권지례를 올렸다.
 40|
 41|“용봉표국의 소국주 주화란이 강호의 선배님들 앞에서 결례를 범했습니다.”
 42|
 43|아픔은 종종 인간을 성숙하게 만들고는 한다. 나는 그녀가 이번 일을 통해 한 단계 성장해졌기를 바랐다.
 44|
 45|‘예상보다 덤덤해 보여서 다행이기는 한데…….’
 46|
 47|뭔가 분위기가 좀, 껄끄럽단 말이지.
 48|
 49|그런 생각을 하고 있을 때, 뭔가가 내 발을 꾸욱 밟았다.
 50|
 51|시선을 내려보니 여인이 신는 화려한 당혜(唐鞋)다.
 52|
 53|내가 알기로 여기서 이런 걸 신을 만한 사람은 단 한 명밖에 없지.
 54|
 55|의문 담긴 눈으로 바라보자 월화가 눈짓으로 좌우를 가리켰다.
 56|
 57|그제야 느껴지는 사람들의 시선들.
 58|
 59|어느새 양옆으로 쫙 갈라진 이들이 나를 뚫어져라 바라보고 있다.
 60|
 61|그리고 그 끝에 포권을 취하고 있는 주화란.
 62|
 63|‘……뭔데, 이거.’
 64|
 65|내 얼굴에 뭐라도 묻었나?
 66|
 67|당황해하는 내게 월화가 들릴락 말락 한 목소리로 속삭였다.
 68|
 69|“진 공자가 한마디 해요.”
 70|
 71|“예?”
 72|
 73|“주 소저가 인사했잖아요. 대표로 받아 줘야지.”
 74|
 75|“아니, 그걸 왜 내가 해요.”
 76|
 77|“얼른. 주 소저 기다리다가 늙겠다.”
 78|
 79|“…….”
 80|
 81|그래, 그사이에 10초 정도 늙긴 했네.
 82|
 83|화산파의 유력 대선 후보, 거지 왕자 궁기방, 하오문 섬서 지부장까지 두고 왜 내가 말해야 하는지는 모르겠지만, 일단 떨떠름한 얼굴로 고개를 꾸벅 숙였다.
 84|
 85|“결례는 무슨. 그리고 저는 강호의 선배 같은 거 아니니까 막 대하셔도 되는데요.”
 86|
 87|“그럴 리 있겠습니까.”
 88|
 89|고개를 든 주화란이 차분하게 말했다.
 90|
 91|“진 대협과 여러 선배님은 용봉표국의 은인들이십니다. 여러분들의 도움이 없었다면 저희 용봉표국은 큰 곤욕을 치렀을 것이고…… 배반자를 처단하지도 못했겠지요.”
 92|
 93|마지막 한마디를 덧붙인 주화란의 표정에 씁쓸함이 스친다.
 94|
 95|그녀도 스스로 그것을 느꼈는지, 이어지는 목소리에는 한층 힘이 실렸다.
 96|
 97|“오늘 입은 은혜는 반드시 갚겠습니다.”
 98|
 99|별거 아니었는데요, 라고 하기에는 확실히 나와 여러 문파의 도움이 컸다. 주화란과 용봉표국 입장에서는 백번 절해도 모자란 수준이다.
100|
101|‘아무리 그래도 대협 소리 듣는 건 좀.’
102|
103|소협도 아직 오글거리는데, 한 단계 진화해 버렸다.
104|
105|나는 어쩐지 수염을 길러야 할 것 같은 기분을 느끼며 말을 돌렸다.
106|
107|“은혜는 저 말고 다른 분들께 갚으시고, 그보다 이제 어쩌실 건가요?”
108|
109|“우선 시신을 수습하고 표국으로 돌아갈 생각이에요. 해결해야 할 일이 많아서요.”
110|
111|“엄청 바쁘시겠네.”
112|
113|의식불명인 아버지 대신 표국을 총괄하는 주화란이다.
114|
115|길었던 표행의 뒤처리만으로도 하루가 금방 갈 텐데, 다이나믹한 사건들까지 잇따랐으니 몸이 열 개라도 부족할 것이 분명했다.
116|
117|내 말에 고개를 끄덕인 주화란이 입을 열었다.
118|
119|“그래도 진 대협 일행을 대접할 만큼의 여유는 있습니다.”
120|
121|“여유가 있다니 그것참 다행…… 예?”
122|
123|“진 대협께서는 저와 식솔들을 구해 주신 은인이십니다. 제대로 된 대접 한번 없이 떠나보낼 수는 없지요.”
124|
125|“어, 주 소저. 그게요.”
126|
127|“혹시, 많이 바쁘신가요?”
128|
129|바쁘지. 상당히 바쁘지.
130|
131|적천강의 치료 기한은 최소 6개월에서 최대 8개월.
132|
133|나는 그 안에 광활한 사천 땅을 뒤져 신의(神醫)라는 정체불명의 인물을 찾아야 한다.
134|
135|‘하남에서 섬서까지 걸린 시간은 일주일. 사천에 당도하려면 아무리 빨라도 또다시 일주일을 이동해야 한다.’
136|
137|그마저도 최대한 신법을 발휘했을 때의 이야기다.
138|
139|신의는 모든 것이 베일에 싸인 인물. 얼만큼의 시간이 소요될지는 누구도 예측할 수 없다.
140|
141|그것이 서안에서 고작 하루를 보내고도 마음이 불안해지는 이유였다.
142|
143|‘오늘도 늦었고.’
144|
145|해가 중천에 뜬 지 오래. 종남파와 얽히는 바람에 상당한 시간을 지체했으니 지금부터라도 발에 불이 나도록 뛰어야 했다.
146|
147|그런데…….
148|
149|“아뇨. 안 바빠요.”
150|
151|나도 모르게 입이 열리더니, 저딴 대답이 튀어나와 버렸다.
152|
153|방금 무슨 일이 벌어진 거지. 이건 원래 하려던 말의 정반대잖아.
154|
155|순간 멍해진 내게 주화란이 조심스럽게 묻는다.
156|
157|“진 대협, 정말 괜찮으신 거 맞아요? 혹시 급한 일이 있으시다면 다음으로 미뤄도 괜찮은데.”
158|
159|감사합니다. 먼저 말 꺼내 주셔서 정말 감사합니다.
160|
161|눈치 빠르고 똑똑한 그녀답다. 가려운 곳을 긁어 주는 말에 나는 망설임 없이 대답했다.
162|
163|“아무리 급해도 밥 한 끼 같이 못 먹겠습니까.”
164|
165|“네에.”
166|
167|“안 그래도 힘을 써서 배고프던 차였는데 잘됐네요. 갑시다.”
168|
169|병신인가, 진짜. 사천에 가야지 용봉표국을 왜 가.
170|
171|하지만 정신을 차렸을 때는 이미 지게를 짊어진 후였다.
172|
173|내심 한숨을 푹 내쉰 그때, 이 모든 상황에서 동떨어져 있던 한 사람이 눈에 들어왔다.
174|
175|물끄러미 바라보자 그가 먼저 입을 연다.
176|
177|“왜, 무슨 할 말이라도 있나?”
178|
179|초면에 반말이 이렇게 자연스럽게 들리기는 처음인데.
180|
181|어쨌든 저쪽에서 먼저 말을 놔 주니 나도 편했다.
182|
183|“그냥. 당신은 안 가나 싶어서.”
184|
185|“일 없다.”
186|
187|“그럼 만들어.”
188|
189|“……?”
190|
191|“어차피 시간 남아도는 거 아니까, 대화나 좀 나누자고.”
192|
193|“대화?”
194|
195|“어, 대화.”
196|
197|눈썹을 치켜세우며 날 바라보던 그, 송일섬이 비스듬히 기대고 있던 몸을 바로 세웠다.
198|
199|
200|
201|* * *
202|
203|
204|
205|초봄. 쨍쨍했던 태양은 용봉표국에 도착한 지 두 시진도 채 되지 않아 서산 뒤로 모습을 감췄다.
206|
207|호롱불이 밝혀진 접객실의 탁자 위에는 진수성찬이 차려졌고, 눈을 휘둥그레 뜬 청풍과 궁기방은 허겁지겁 음식들을 입 안으로 쑤셔 넣었다.
208|
209|“쩝쩝. 으닌. 이거 마시써요. 쩝쩝쩝.”
210|
211|“……많이 먹어. 가급적 말은 하지 말고.”
212|
213|맛있어 보이긴 했다.
214|
215|청풍이 굳이 입 안에 든 걸 보여 주기 전까지는.
216|
217|“와구와구. 이 표국 음식 잘하네. 소국주. 혹시 본 방의 식구들에게도 남는 음식을 나눠 줄 수 있겠소?”
218|
219|궁기방, 저 자식은 진짜 뼛속까지 거지다.
220|
221|고기 위주로 학살 중인 녀석을 향해 주화란이 고개를 끄덕였다.
222|
223|“물론이죠. 배가 고프면 얼마든지 찾아오라고 하세요.”
224|
225|“오, 얼마든지?”
226|

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
